newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's windfall tax to affect BT - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's windfall tax to affect BT - paper.

text.p: A proposed windfall tax by Britain's opposition Labour party would apply to all privatised utilities whose business is licensed and regulated by statute, according to legislation being prepared by the party, said the Financial Times newspaper.

This means that British Telecommunications, airports operator BAA, Associated British Ports, Railtrack and British Gas would all be liable if Labour win the forthcoming election, said the paper which claimed to have obtained details of the legislative preparations.

British Airways would be excluded despite widespread speculation that it would pay the tax. It will come as a shock to many larger companies who have assumed the levy would be focused on electricity and water businesses, said the article.
The wide scope of the tax will allow Labour to raise up to 10 billion pounds ($16 billion) while arguing it is not placing an excessive burden on a limited number of companies.
On Thursday Gordon Brown, the shadow chancellor, made clear that the minimum target was 3 billion pounds to create work for the young and long term unemployed.
